newsitem.title: FINLAND: POSTIPANKKI SEES CLEAR FULL-YEAR 1996 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: POSTIPANKKI SEES CLEAR FULL-YEAR 1996 PROFIT.

text.p: Finnish state-owned banking group Postipankki Oy said on Wednesday it expects to maintain its January-Septemebr profit trend for the rest of year.
"We expect the profit trend to be maintained throughout the rest of the year," Postipankki said in a statement with its nine-month results.
The group's full-year result will show a clear profit, it said.
Postipankki said profits from securities transactions lifted its January-September earnings.

"The 477 million markka profit on securities transactions resulted mainly from profits on the sale of bonds, and as valuation and realised gains on other treasury products," Postipankki said, noting that in January-September 1995 it had a 340 million markka loss from securites transactions.
Postpankki's January-September report showed a 537 million markka operating profit after credit losses, up from a 332 million markka loss in the first nine months of 1995.
Postipankki said a fall in credit losses to 187 million markka from 345 million helped its nine-month earnings.

The January-September profits were hampered by a fall in income from financial operations and by 143 million markka in additional depreciation and write-offs made on the bank's real estate and shares in real estate corporations, Postipankki said.
Consolidated net income from financial operations fell to 1.50 billion markka in January-September from 1.65 billion markka in the year-ago period.
"The main reason was the narrower interest margin caused by falling interest rates", it said
Postipankki said write-offs on securities rose to 115 million markka in January-Septmember from zero in the first nine months in 1995, and depreciation rose to 187 million markka from 145 million.
